description:
FILED s514 (Fable, 2026-10-10 10:45) from s514a's member-1 report (worktree agent-a758d6e41f15d3c26, scratch/s514a/STOP.md, load ~4.7 at measurement).  The shims (#2947) are CORRECT (byte-identical digests) and are the right layer by rule 9a (a user can write a digest in Perl), so they ship.  The COST: pure Perl under PCL runs the compression function 400-2000x slower than XS -- a 100 MB file = ~50 s for MD5, ~7 min for SHA-512 (perl: 0.1-0.2 s).  OPTIONS, in order of cost: (a) accept, document the ratio in docs/shipped-modules.md (done by s514a) -- fine for the everyday battery and small inputs; (b) a generic runtime primitive `builtin::digest_octets(ALG, OCTETS)` (and an incremental state pair) that the shims call for the compression work while keeping perl's API, aliases, base64 and error shapes in Perl: MD5 via SBCL's `sb-md5` contrib (already in every SBCL), SHA-1/SHA-2 as ~200 lines of typed Lisp (ironclad is not vendored and must not become a dependency); the primitive is generic (an ALG name), no module name in cl/ -- the Time::HiRes / POSIX builtin:: seam pattern; (c) nothing else.  The decision is the USER's (a `cl/` primitive for a non-core module is the rule-9a boundary case: "only what no Perl can say" -- here Perl CAN say it, just slowly).  Measure first on a real program (a checksum of a 10 MB file) before deciding; the shim's profile under statprof says where the time goes (expected: the 32-bit masking `& 0xffffffff` and the rotate on every step -- a `use integer` + typed path in the compiler could also narrow the gap WITHOUT a primitive: measure that first, it is the general lever).

USER RULING 2026-10-10 11:14: "We are going to look at XS after we get PCL less buggy, so just note the speed problem and see if we can get XS to work."  => this task is PARKED: option (a) accept + document (done by s514a in docs/shipped-modules.md) is the state; options (b) a builtin:: digest primitive and the `use integer` typing lever are NOT scheduled.  The resolution path is the XS bridge (pclxs, parked since s485, memory project_xs_shim_design; the three Pl/t/xs-0N.t files skip_all) -- when XS works again, perl's own Digest::MD5 / Digest::SHA XS builds replace the shims (the shim-vs-XS precedence is docs/ir-spec.md Â§9).  Revisit trigger: the XS revisit, or a USER request for a fast digest before it.  DECIDED ## s514 has the line.
